A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GraphInsight work. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original GraphSQA experiments across five LLMs, including baseline comparisons, component ablations, composite-task results, and sensitivity studies.

after.justification: v3 retains original GraphSQA experiments and additionally reports GraphToken comparisons and detailed task-level results.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same PageRank-based description reorganization, GraphRAG construction and retrieval, and integration into multi-step reasoning. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same GraphSQA task coverage, and all 20 appendix task templates match substantively. The added triangle-task description corresponds to the existing connected-neighbor-pairs task. Changing the main-text composite-task count from eight to seven does not establish changed coverage; Appendix A still says eight.

E2.justification: v3 adds GraphToken as a tenth baseline and reports its overall, macro, and micro scores for all five LLMs in Table 1. The previous nine comparators remain; the new appendix heatmaps use the original comparator set.

E3.justification: Both retain the stated 15–200-node evaluation, 10,400 tasks, boolean scoring, numerical relative-error scoring, and Jaccard scoring. The reported method settings and sensitivity sweeps also remain unchanged. More specific checkpoint names provide documentation rather than evidence of changed models or protocols.

E4.justification: Table 2 revises the reported evidence for reorganization's macro-level contribution in four models. The component-ablation conditions and the alpha, beta, and GraphRAG-rate sensitivity analyses remain the same; no new robustness scenario is introduced.

E5.justification: Both state that reported values average three runs. The Wilcoxon signed-rank analysis is retained unchanged, including statistic 0.0 and p-value 6.103515625 × 10^-5, moving from Appendix F to G. No new uncertainty-reporting practice is introduced.

E6.justification: v3 substantially expands reported results with task-level score breakdowns across five LLMs, a ranking table, and GraphToken scores (Figures 8–12 and Tables 1 and 4). Four macro reorganization scores change in Table 2, including Llama-3-8B from 0.5422 to 0.5029 and Vicuna-7B from 0.2296 to 0.1571. All pre-existing Table 1 scores remain unchanged; the PDFs do not explain these revisions as reruns.

T1.justification: The graph-description definitions, positional-bias assumption, KL objective, PageRank equation, retrieval mathematics, and metric formulas retain their substance. Writing CLLM(T) instead of CLLM and renumbering equations are notation and presentation changes, with no new proof or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about positional bias, GraphInsight's two techniques, GraphSQA, and superior graph-understanding performance. Added comparisons do not produce a substantive revision of these central claims.

C2.justification: The new Limitations section adds task-dependent importance measurement and retrieval-efficiency/storage tradeoffs, and discusses combining GraphInsight with instruction fine-tuning or implicit embeddings. The earlier discussion of uncertain U-shaped comprehension and PageRank limitations remains in the appendix.

D1.justification: The new appendix results specify checkpoints more precisely, including Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 and vicuna-7b-v1.1, where v2 used broader model labels. Hardware, software versions, hyperparameters, and task templates are retained, without establishing an actual implementation change.

R1.justification: v3 adds Graphwiz and LLM4DyG references and a benchmark-comparison table. It also explicitly positions GraphToken's implicit GNN embeddings as orthogonal to GraphInsight's explicit descriptions. The main research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v3 corrects typos and tightens several related-work, setup, and conclusion passages. It adds a Limitations section and an appendix results subsection, while retaining the main section sequence and most explanatory prose.

P2.justification: The main text and technical appendices change from single-column to two-column presentation, extensively resizing and repositioning existing displays. Table 1 gains a GraphToken column, and v3 adds the benchmark-comparison table, ranking table, and five task-level heatmap figures.

improvement.justification: GraphToken comparisons, task-level results, checkpoint identifiers, and concrete limitations improve breadth and transparency. However, v3 changes Table 2 macro scores without reconciling them with Table 1. Its new Table 4 places GraphInsight fourth for Llama-3-8B macro tasks while Section 5.2.1 cites that table as supporting superiority across all models. These unexplained empirical conflicts offset the useful additions, preventing a reliable judgment of net quality improvement.
